title: A multi-subpopulation cooperative evolutionary particle swarm optimization method for 3D orthodontic path planning
html: Orthodontic path planning is a key component of 3D tooth movement simulation, directly affecting the rationality and computational efficiency of tooth movement planning. However, complex 3D tooth movement scenarios involve high-dimensional trajectory optimization and repeated collision evaluation, while still suffering from insufficient path search, excessive cumulative translational and rotational movement, and susceptibility to local optima. To address these issues, this paper proposes a 3D orthodontic path-planning method based on multi-subpopulation cooperative evolutionary particle swarm optimization (CLEPSO). First, in the particle swarm initialization stage, linear interpolation combined with dual cosine and sine perturbations is adopted to enhance population diversity and reduce the risk of premature convergence. Second, during the iterative process, particles are divided into high-quality particles, medium-quality particles, and low-quality particles according to particle quality, and differentiated exploration strategies are implemented to improve global exploration and local exploitation capabilities. In addition, a subpopulation collaboration and information-sharing mechanism is proposed to enhance the algorithm’s ability to reduce the risk of local stagnation. Finally, the method is validated using nine benchmark test functions and orthodontic cases involving dental arches. Compared with MSIPSO, CLEPSO reduces the total translational displacement of the maxillary and mandibular arches by 12.55 mm and 6.05 mm, respectively. Compared with several mainstream methods, the proposed algorithm demonstrates better overall performance in convergence speed, convergence accuracy, tooth translation, and tooth rotation. These results indicate that CLEPSO can effectively generate 3D tooth movement paths satisfying the predefined movement and collision constraints.
